title: Qonclave capability grant
description: A signed, scoped, time-boxed authorization issued by a hub allowing one node to talk to a specific target. Generalizes the Direct-Bind broker in ARCHITECTURE.md §3 and SECURITY.md §3 to three audience types: an external operator, a compute node, or a PEER HUB. The audience verifies the grant offline against the issuer's pinned CA root — a mesh that needs the issuing hub online to authorize failover has not failed over.

grant_id.description: Unique id, also the handle used for revocation.

issuer.description: The hub that minted this grant, acting as local CA (SECURITY.md §3).

subject.description: The node being authorized — normally an edge device.

audience.description: The specific target the subject may talk to. A grant is valid for exactly one audience; presenting it elsewhere MUST fail.

tenant_id.description: Tenant this grant operates within. A verifier MUST reject a grant whose tenant_id differs from its own unless cross_tenant is explicitly true.

cross_tenant.description: Deny by default. Setting this true is the only way to authorize across the isolation boundary asserted in SECURITY.md §2, and is expected to be rare and audited.

scope.description: Operations the subject may perform against the audience. A verifier MUST reject any operation not listed.
